surface: The time editor, a native time input over the cell: opening it, typing a time, Enter committing it, and Escape cancelling a second edit.

steps.note: Enter opens the editor on the Time cell (`9:30 AM`) and focuses its native time input, which holds 09:30. Required: the control, in the reader's words: the hour segment the focus lands on (NVDA `Hours, spin button, 09`, VoiceOver `hour stepper` or `Hours stepper`). `time` is not a synonym, because the column is named Time and a reader that reads the cell would satisfy it. Finding: VoiceOver says nothing when the time editor opens, on both browsers, and reads the stepper only when the editor opens a second time (the reopen step); the date editor records the same silence.

Four digits fill the hour and the minute of the input in Chromium and Firefox (11:45; the AM or PM segment keeps its value). WebKit's time input does not move to the next segment, so the digits overwrite each other and the commit gives 12:30 AM: on VoiceOver with WebKit the groups of the next steps that name the typed time fail for the input, not for the reading. Nothing is required here: a reader speaks a segment's new value in its own words (NVDA `AM slash PM, spin button`, VoiceOver `AM AM/PM stepper`).

Enter commits the time and moves the selection one row down (enterMoves), to the next row's Time, drawn as `10:15 AM`. Required: that cell's value and its row. Finding: the focus stays on the closed time input, as the date editor leaves it, so no reader reads the cell: NVDA with Chromium reads the input's AM/PM segment, NVDA with Firefox says nothing, and VoiceOver reads a stepper of the hidden input (`10 hour stepper` with WebKit, `AM AM/PM stepper` with Chromium).

ArrowUp moves to the edited cell, drawn as `11:45 AM` (`12:30 AM` in WebKit, see the typing step); the arrow key takes the focus from the closed input to the cell, and NVDA and VoiceOver with Chromium read it.
The editor opens again, on the new value, and every reader names the hour segment this time.
Escape closes the editor without a change. Finding: no reader says anything, on any browser, and the focus stays on the closed input, as the commit leaves it.
